paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. The crowds come running because of what they've heard Jesus is doing, and they press in so hard He needs a boat (Mark 3:8-10). Even the unclean spirits know exactly who He is, and they cry out, "You are the Son of God!" (Mark 3:11). But knowing who Jesus is and following Him are two different things, and the passage shows us both.

Then look at what Jesus does on the mountain. He "called for those He wanted, and they came to Him" (Mark 3:13). The first job He gives the twelve is "to accompany Him," and only after that comes being sent out to preach and having authority to drive out demons (Mark 3:14-15). Being with Jesus comes first, friend. I got pulled out of a junk drawer, so I can tell you the best part of being called is who is doing the calling.

Jesus picks out Simon and gives him the name Peter, and He gives the brothers James and John the name Boanerges, "Sons of Thunder" (Mark 3:16-17). He knows each one of them by name. And right at the end of the list is Judas Iscariot, "who betrayed Jesus" (Mark 3:19). That part is heavy, and I think it's there to be honest with us: being near Jesus is a gift, and it calls for a heart that stays with Him. So baker, you've been called to the Word too. Come close, stay close, and let Him make you ready.
